claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi, the Cantor high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has high configurational entropy and significant configurational disorder.
High configurational entropy intrinsically produces sluggish diffusion in CrMnFeCoNi.
The proposed sluggish-diffusion effect reduces the mobility of oxygen and metal ions at high temperature.
Transport through the alloy, across the oxide/metal interface, and through the oxide layer contributes to high-temperature oxidation behavior.
Reduced oxygen and cation diffusivity causes CrMnFeCoNi to develop a thinner, more coherent, and less defective oxide layer.
A thinner, more coherent oxide layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
Slower diffusion limits rapid oxide thickening and oxide-defect formation.
Slower diffusion leads to a stable, protective oxide scale on the Cantor alloy.
Lower-entropy alloys have higher diffusion rates than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Higher diffusion rates in lower-entropy alloys produce thicker, more defective, and less protective oxide layers.
Relative to a lower-entropy comparator, CrMnFeCoNi will show lower oxidation weight gain.
Relative to a lower-entropy comparator, CrMnFeCoNi will form a thinner and more uniform oxide scale.
Relative to a lower-entropy comparator, CrMnFeCoNi will exhibit slower oxidation kinetics.
The proposed behavior is applicable to oxidation in air at approximately 1000–1100 degrees Celsius.
Oxygen partial pressure can change the oxidation products and oxidation behavior of equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
A lower-entropy binary or ternary comparator can be made closely matched to the equiatomic five-component alloy in overall reactive-element composition.
Differences in composition or secondary-phase formation in the comparator could affect diffusion independently of configurational entropy.
Comparable or better oxidation kinetics, scale thickness, uniformity, or phase composition in the lower-entropy comparator would falsify configurational entropy as the primary source of protection.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes protection in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi to sluggish diffusion and a stable scale, whereas cited same-system evidence reports vigorous oxidation, highly mobile Mn, pore formation, accelerated oxide growth, absence of a protective Cr2O3 barrier, and formation of non-protective Mn-rich oxides.

The comparator is described both as a binary or ternary alloy and as closely composition-matched to equiatomic five-component CrMnFeCoNi with similar reactive-element composition. Removing two or three principal elements necessarily changes the overall composition, so configurational entropy is not cleanly isolated.

The structural-mediator field says the oxide-layer structure is mediated by reduced diffusivity, placing diffusion upstream of the structural mediator, while the stated field sequence implies a mediator-to-mechanism link. The causal content is coherent only if reduced diffusion is treated as the mechanism and oxide structure as its consequence.
